scope.summary: Bind BodyKit to the kernel sandbox per Section 13.27: model-authored body generation and validation execute in the kernel sandbox at process tier with fs-only capabilities — network and process-spawn attempts fail closed — and sandbox run receipts link to the body draft they produced.
acceptance_criteria: author_body, randomize_body, corrective bakes, and validation runs for model-authored drafts execute inside the kernel sandbox at process tier with the fs-only capability set (scoped workdir, no network, no arbitrary exec).
Escape attempts fail closed in test: a sandboxed task attempting a network connection or process spawn is denied and the denial is recorded on the run receipt.
Every sandbox run emits a receipt linked to the body draft (run id, capability set, exit status, artifact hashes); promotion evidence can cite the sandbox lineage.
Sandbox failures (crash, timeout) mark the draft's validation state typed-failed rather than leaving orphaned intermediate files (cleanup verified).
The Blender-bridge export path documents its OWN process boundary relative to this sandbox tier (bridge runs are jobs, not sandbox-bypasses).
scope.risk_if_missed: Model-generated body code paths run with kernel privileges — one prompt-injected or buggy generation task gets filesystem-wide or network reach, a direct kernel-security regression against the established sandbox architecture.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Backend/solver scope: behavior is observable via TraceProjection, typed TAILOR_BODY_* receipts, and the 13.12 capture APIs; operator/model GUI exposure rides the BodyKit panes (13.27) and is validated there.

target_entries: Tailor UserManual > BodyKit jobs, diagnostics, and recovery

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: This MT owns authoritative, job, or external-tool lifecycle events and must project the same event_id, run_id, actor_id, and correlation_id from EventLedger into Flight Recorder.
This MT must wire the shared internal_diagnostics API for its native, job, device, solver-run, or DCC failure modes with bounded structured evidence.
The owning native shell or scheduled job supplies Palmistry coverage; this MT must preserve operation identity and recovery handles.

risks: Broad MT scope can hide multiple review targets.
Markdown MT lists may disagree with packet-declared active/next MT truth.
Receipt routing may target an old MT if contract identity is omitted.
minimum_controls: Exactly one primary proof target per MT unless the packet records why not.
MT identity must be stable and referenced by receipt correlation.
Generated projection drift must not wake Coder or Validator by itself.

required_changes_before_execution: Consume the signed technical refinement, canonical command/surface registries, classified HBR tiers, and task-oriented UserManual contract before execution.
